t:
Section 372 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
    (1) by striking “(a) In General.—”; and 
    (2) by striking subsection (b).

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to 10 U.S.C. 372, striking a subsection heading and subsection (b). It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. There is no tempting participation reading, since no outside party or decision process is mentioned.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely technical amendment to the United States Code, removing specific subsections from a statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It merely changes the text of the law without creating new participatory mechanisms.
qwen_block.s: Section 372 of title 10, United States Code, is amended— (1) by striking “(a) In General.—”; and (2) by striking subsection (b).

opus.w: This section only makes technical amendments: it strikes a subsection heading and deletes subsection (b) of 10 U.S.C. 372. No outside party (state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public) is consulted, heard or given a role in any federal decision. Guessing what the deleted subsection contained would go beyond the text and could not change that answer, since the amendment involves no outside-party process.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Someone could assume that the struck subsection (b) of 10 U.S.C. § 372 dealt with consultation or coordination with outside parties. That reading fails because the section text only makes technical amendments. It removes a heading and deletes a subsection without describing either one. Nothing in the text involves any party outside the federal government in a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends an existing statute by deleting specific subsections. It does not establish any advisory committees, public comment periods, consultations with non-federal entities, or rights to sue. The text describes a legislative change to the code, not a procedural requirement for outside participation in a federal decision.
qwen_chat.s: Section 372 of title 10, United States Code, is amended— (1) by striking “(a) In General.—”; and (2) by striking subsection (b).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that amending a statute could implicitly involve participation if the original statute contained participation mechanisms, but this section only removes text. It does not create any new process for outside involvement.
